papers.title_in_file: A Transferable Machine Learning Approach to Predict Quantum Circuit Parameters for Electronic Structure Problems
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, methodology, evaluation, discussion and conclusion; appendices skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A study that trains neural networks (GAT and SchNet variants) to predict VQE circuit parameters for hydrogen chains and rings, tested on larger molecules than those in training.

assertions.value: The authors report parameter prediction for hydrogenic systems that is transferable to instances larger than the training instances, generalizing to unseen system sizes up to H12.
quotes: we show parameter prediction that is systematically transferable to instances significantly larger than the training instances.
These have shown success in modeling the circuit parameters of hydrogenic systems, generalizing for unseen system sizes up to H12.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on simulated hydrogenic systems.
assertions.reader_inference: The test molecules are minimal-basis hydrogen systems, so transfer to other molecules is not shown.

assertions.value: The authors state that the evaluation used datasets of 500 random instances with molecule sizes from H2 to H12, in a minimal basis with one orbital, or two qubits, for each hydrogen atom.
quotes: For the evaluation we produced several datasets of 500 random instances with varying molecule sizes (ranging from H2 to H12).
Here we chose a minimal basis approach (one orbital, or two qubits, for each hydrogen atom)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own evaluation setup, Section II.A.

assertions.value: The authors report that the mixed SchNet model, trained on a smaller mixed dataset, improved accuracy on ring instances by one order of magnitude compared with the linear SchNet model.
assertions.anchor: Section III.A Random Instance Evaluation, results on ring instances
quotes: Comparing this results with the linear SchNet ones shows that the accuracy improved by one order of magnitude, which is remarkable given the size of the training set.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study; figure-based comparison.

assertions.value: The authors state that the work focuses on hydrogenic systems, which they describe as relatively simple to treat, and that the largest amount of energy outliers for the SchNet-based model occurs for the H12 system.
quotes: In this work, we focus on hydrogenic systems because they are relatively simple to treat
the largest amount of energy outliers occur for the H12 system
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its scope in Section II.A; the outlier statement is an observed result.
assertions.reader_inference: Extension to non-hydrogenic molecules is left to future work.

papers.title_in_file: The Design and Implementation of a Quantum Information Science Undergraduate Program
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, program development, pedagogy, success factors, conclusion and appendix 1 and 2.
papers.what_it_is: A description of how Universite de Sherbrooke designed and launched an undergraduate degree in quantum information science for quantum software developers.

assertions.value: The authors state that Universite de Sherbrooke created and launched an undergraduate degree in quantum information science to address the talent gap, training quantum software developers in three and a half years.
quotes: responded by creating and launching an innovative undergraduate degree in quantum information science, aiming to address this gap by training quantum software developers in three and a half years.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors describe their own program, Abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that the acceleration of quantum computing R&D has faced a major bottleneck in the past few years: a lack of available highly qualified personnel.
quotes: This acceleration of R&D in quantum computing has faced a major bottleneck in the past few years: a lack of available highly qualified personnel
assertions.certainty_reason: Author claim citing other work, not shown in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors report that since its launch in 2022 the program has grown to three active cohorts with over 50 enrolled students, and that student feedback has been overwhelmingly positive.
quotes: Since its launch in 2022, the program has grown to have three active cohorts with over 50 enrolled students.
Student feedback has been overwhelmingly positive, with a particular appreciation for the integrative project courses.
assertions.certainty_reason: Self-reported program outcome; no survey data shown.
assertions.reader_inference: No evaluation data or survey method is given in the conclusion.

assertions.value: The authors cite a 2022 study by the Quantum Economic Development Consortium, based on an earlier survey, as showing that most jobs in the field do not require a PhD.
quotes: A 2022 study by the Quantum Economic Development Consortium based on an earlier survey also showed that most jobs in the field do not require a PhD
assertions.certainty_reason: Result the paper attributes to other work.

papers.title_in_file: The Robustness Verification of Linear Sound Quantum Classifiers
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, background, formalizations, verification section (definitions and proof outline), implementation and results.
papers.what_it_is: A single-author method for verifying the robustness of quantum classifiers that satisfy a Linear Sound Property, demonstrated on a QCNN classifying MNIST digits.

assertions.value: The author presents a quick and sound method for the robustness verification of quantum classifiers that are Linear Sound, and reports implementing it with a Quantum Convolutional Neural Network in MindQuantum and successfully verifying its robustness when classifying the MNIST dataset.
quotes: I present a quick and sound method for the robustness verification of a sort of quantum classifiers who are Linear Sound.
successfully verified its robustness when classifying MNIST dataset.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author claim backed by one simulated demonstration; soundness argued in Section 3.
assertions.reader_inference: The soundness argument is given in prose and geometry; the demonstration is on a small simulated binary task.

assertions.value: The paper defines a classifier as having the Linear Sound Property if, whenever two states are classified into the same class, any convex combination of them is classified into the same class too.
quotes: We say a classifier have the Linear Sound Property, LSP, if and only if it satisfies:
if states 1, 2 are classified into the same class
assertions.certainty_reason: Definition 6, Section 3.

assertions.value: The author states that the MNIST data were filtered to binary classification only, using an amplitude encoder on 8 qubits, and reports over 90% classification accuracy on the test dataset for the simple QCNN.
quotes: Due to the limitation on the capability of classical computers to simulate quantum circuit, I filtered the dataset to do the binary classification only
to simulate 8 qubits
over 90% accuracy of classfication on the test dataset
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the limit and setup in Section 4.1; the accuracy figure is a measured result.
assertions.reader_inference: The verification was run on a simulated two-class problem only.

papers.title_in_file: Biclustering a dataset using photonic quantum computing
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results summary, future work and conclusion; method sections skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A proposal and simulation study applying boson sampling and Gaussian boson sampling to the biclustering problem on synthetic datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report that their simulations of the proposed heuristics show promising results for future exploration, and that they conducted four preliminary tests on synthetic datasets.
quotes: Our simulations for the above proposed heuristics show promising results for future exploration in this area.
Being the first work in this research direction, we conducted four preliminary tests where we simulated the application of these quantum computing models on synthetic datasets for biclustering.
assertions.certainty_reason: Preliminary simulation results from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that both boson sampling and GBS perform better when the contrast between the values inside and outside the bicluster is large, and that the GBS approach seems to produce comparable or better results with fewer samples.
assertions.anchor: Section 6.5 A short summary of the results
quotes: Both boson sampling and GBS perform better when the contrast between the values that are inside and outside the bicluster is large.
The GBS approach seems to produce comparable or better results for fewer number of samples
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation results from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that if multiple biclusters are present within a dataset, their chances of being detected goes down.
assertions.anchor: Section 6.5 A short summary of the results
quotes: If multiple biclusters are present within a dataset, then their chances of being detected goes down.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limit, Section 6.5.

assertions.value: The authors state that at the time of writing there was no publicly available hardware that would support problems of the sizes used in their work, so the results come from simulation.
quotes: At the time of writing, there was no publicly available hardware that would support problems of the sizes like the ones in this work.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limit, Section 7.

papers.title_in_file: A Systematic Study of Noise Effects in Hybrid Quantum-Classical Machine Learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, methodology, experimental setup, results sections A to C and conclusion.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of a variational quantum classifier on the Titanic dataset under combined dataset-level noise and circuit-level quantum noise.

assertions.value: The authors report that under ideal execution, with no dataset-level perturbation and no circuit noise, the variational quantum classifier achieved a mean training accuracy of 76.40% and a mean testing accuracy of 76.12%.
quotes: the variational quantum classifier achieved a mean training accuracy of 76.40% and a closely matching mean testing accuracy of 76.12%.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulated study on one dataset.

assertions.value: The authors report that introducing circuit-level quantum noise reduced mean training accuracy from approximately 76% to 38.67% and mean testing accuracy to 39.15%, with amplitude damping the most severe channel.
assertions.anchor: Section V.B Impact of circuit-level quantum noise
quotes: meant training accuracy collapsed from approximately 76% to 38.67%, while mean testing accuracy droped to 39.15%.
Among the four quantum noise channels, amplitude damping consistently exhibited the most severe impact on both loss convergence and final accuracy.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulated study.

assertions.value: The authors state that noise in classical input data can significantly intensify the effects of quantum decoherence, resulting in less stable training and noticeably lower classification accuracy.
quotes: noise in classical input data can significantly intensify the effects of quantum decoherence, resulting in less stable training and noticeably lower classification accuracy.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulated study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the experimental evaluation is limited to small-scale quantum circuits, relies on noise simulation, and that validation on real quantum hardware remains future work.
assertions.anchor: Section VI Conclusion and future work
quotes: While the experimental evaluation is limited to smallscale quantum circuits
Although this study relies on high-fidelity noise simulation, validating these findings on real quantum hardware remains an important direction for future work.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limit, Section VI.

papers.title_in_file: Applying the quantum approximate optimization algorithm to general constraint satisfaction problems
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, main results list, numerical results summary and conclusions; the long derivations in Sections III and IV and the appendices were not read line by line.
papers.what_it_is: A theory and numerics paper computing the success probability of one-layer QAOA on random boolean constraint satisfaction problems and comparing the scaling with the classical solver MapleSAT.

assertions.value: The authors state that their techniques compute the success probability of QAOA with one layer and given parameters on randomly generated constraint satisfaction instances in time polynomial in n and k.
quotes: Our techniques allow us to compute the success probability of QAOA with one layer and given parameters, when applied to randomly generated instances of CSPs with k binary variables per constraint, in time polynomial in n and k.
assertions.certainty_reason: Derived algorithm and formulae, Sections III and IV.

assertions.value: The authors report that for all the problems considered, the scaling of MapleSAT appears to be more efficient than the scaling of QAOA, and that random k-SAT seems the most promising for demonstrating a quantum-classical separation.
assertions.anchor: Section I main results, point 2; Section VI
quotes: We find that, for all the problems considered, the scaling of MapleSAT appears to be more efficient than the scaling of QAOA.
None of the problems we considered demonstrated an improved running time scaling of QAOA when compared with MapleSAT
assertions.certainty_reason: Runtime scaling estimated numerically; MapleSAT scaling determined experimentally.

assertions.value: The authors state that they focus on QAOA with only one layer, which is easier to analyse than the general case, and that whether the relative difficulty of the CSP families holds for higher p cannot be answered conclusively with their techniques.
quotes: Here we will focus on the case of QAOA with only one layer (p = 1).
A key question which cannot be answered conclusively with our techniques is whether the relative difficulty of the families of CSPs considered would be maintained for higher p.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated scope and limit, Sections I and VI.

papers.title_in_file: Circuit Harmonic Matrices: A Spectral Framework for Quantum Machine Learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, discussion and limitations, outlook; derivation sections II to V and the numerical experiments were skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that maps parametrised quantum circuits to an architecture matrix, linking circuit structure to feature correlations and training-kernel geometry without reference to data.

assertions.value: The authors state that they introduce a data-agnostic framework that maps a broad family of circuits into a single architecture matrix, and that kernel structure and coefficient statistics can be reconstructed analytically from circuit design alone.
quotes: We introduce a data-agnostic framework, one requiring no knowledge of a training dataset or optimisation trajectory, that maps a broad family of circuits into a single architecture matrix built over learnable features and parameters.
kernel structure and coefficient statistics can be reconstructed analytically from circuit design alone, without reference to a dataset or optimisation trajectory.
assertions.certainty_reason: Analytic factorisations derived in Sections III to V.

assertions.value: The authors state that the framework is developed for the Quantum Fourier Model setting with commuting phase-style encoders, and that architectures with non-commuting feature maps may not admit the same finite harmonic description without modification.
assertions.anchor: Section VII.A Assumptions and limitations, item 1
quotes: The framework is developed for the Quantum Fourier Model setting, where commuting phase-style encoders yield a finite encoder-accessible input spectrum and an explicit harmonic factorisation of the learned function.
Architectures employing non-commuting feature maps or qualitatively different data-loading schemes may not admit the same finite harmonic description without modification.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section VII.A, limitation 1.

assertions.value: The authors state that the parameter-averaged objects are best interpreted as initialisation-time characterisations of a circuit's architectural prior, not the statistics of a trained model.
quotes: are therefore best interpreted as initialisation-time characterisations of a circuit
assertions.certainty_reason: Section VII.A, limitation 4.

assertions.value: The authors state that the numerical results should be interpreted as evidence that the predicted structures are visible in compute-limited regimes, rather than as demonstrations of convergence to the full, untruncated objects.
quotes: The numerical results in this paper should be interpreted as evidence that the predicted structures are visible in compute-limited regimes, rather than as demonstrations of convergence to the full, untruncated objects.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section VII.A, numerical limitations.

papers.title_in_file: QUBO-based SVM for credit card fraud detection on a real QPU
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, conclusion and results section; method sections and result plots skimmed. Result figures are images.
papers.what_it_is: A study that trains an SVM reformulated as a QUBO problem on a neutral atom QPU and on simulations, tested on a credit card fraud dataset.

assertions.value: The authors state that one of their proposed QUBO SVM versions seems to achieve higher performance and lower errors than popular machine learning models, and that data obtained via a real QPU extend up to 24 atoms.
quotes: We show that one of our proposed versions seems to achieve higher performance and lower errors
the data obtained via real QPU extend up to 24 atoms
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study; the numerical results are in figures not quoted here.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract hedges with the word seems.

assertions.value: The authors state that each configuration was trained and tested on 10 different splits of the dataset, and that simulations used training sets of 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 samples with quantum registers of 8, 10, 12, 14 and 16 atoms.
quotes: each configuration was trained and tested on 10 different splits of the dataset finally calculating mean and standard deviation of the chosen metrics.
these analyses were performed by running ideal and non-ideal simulations with training sets of 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 samples, using quantum registers of 8, 10, 12, 14 and 16 atoms, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup, Section 9.
assertions.reader_inference: The training sets are very small, so the comparison with classical models is on small training sets.

assertions.value: The authors report that simulations at different noise levels showed improvements in the presence of noise compared to the ideal case.
quotes: compared simulations at different noise levels, showing improvements in the presence of noise compared to the ideal case.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that their approach requires only the training part to use a QPU, while the testing phase uses classical hardware.
quotes: Our approach, on the other hand, requires that only the training part exploits a QPU, while the testing phase exploits classical hardware.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope, Section 1.
